notes: Read against the snippet at ca4fc84 (src/models/snippets-batch-e.ts) and the demo entry (src/models/batch-e.ts). Description: JS makes forty flakes once, each with random depth, speed (--t) and drift, one CSS animation (fall) does the falling and perspective makes near flakes big and fast: all true. How: the per-flake properties (--x, --z, --s, --o, --drift, --t, --d) and that JS does nothing after; the fall from -53cqh to 185cqh at the flake's own translateZ, the night a size container (container-type: size) so cqh/cqw are shares of the canvas; drift as --drift x 0.33cqw, "a plain number which CSS counts in shares of the canvas width"; depth and size as plain numbers times --u; negative delays so it is snowing on the first frame; trees at translateZ -240/-140/-20 units in the same preserve-3d world hiding far flakes; the night inset: 0 in percentages. The claim that a flake placed in shares stays at the same share on every canvas shape was confirmed by eye and measure (seeded, 1:1 vs 16:9 vs 9:16, offsets under 0.5% of the canvas). Technique chips and tags (generated, loop, particles, scene, weather) fit. No change needed.
